## Summary

I identified the canonical human UniProt entries, retrieved their sequences, and computed masses independently (Biopython), cross-checking against the UniProt record, EBI Proteins API, and NCBI RefSeq.

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Computed mass |
|------|---------|--------|---------------|
| AOAH | P28039 | 575 aa | **65.10 kDa** |
| ZNF219 | Q9P2Y4 | 722 aa | **76.88 kDa** |

**ZNF219 is heavier** (76.88 vs 65.10 kDa, a difference of ~11.8 kDa).

**Important data caveat:** UniProt's `P28039` record carries stale metadata (`length: 719`, `molWeight: 81381`), which contradicts its own sequence string. The sequence string is 575 aa and its MD5/CRC64 checksums match the record, the chain feature boundaries (157–575) fit a 575-aa precursor, the EBI Proteins API reports 575 aa / 65,105 Da, and NCBI RefSeq NP_001628 (AOAH isoform a) is 575 aa. So 65.10 kDa is the correct value; the 81.4 kDa figure is an artifact. Note also that AOAH is cleaved into a ~15 kDa small subunit and a ~50 kDa large subunit (mature heterodimer), but the precursor mass is what's compared here. ZNF219 was confirmed at 722 aa across all three RefSeq variants (NP_001095924, NP_001095142, NP_057507).

<solution>
ZNF219 (UniProt Q9P2Y4, 722 aa) has a computed mass of **76.88 kDa**, while AOAH (UniProt P28039, 575 aa) has a computed mass of **65.10 kDa**. ZNF219 is therefore the heavier protein by ~11.8 kDa.

Note: the UniProt record for P28039 lists stale metadata (719 aa / 81,381 Da) that conflicts with its own 575-aa sequence; the 575-aa/65.1 kDa value was confirmed via checksum match, chain-feature boundaries, the EBI Proteins API (65,105 Da), and NCBI RefSeq NP_001628.
